name: Books & Authors
summary: Ancient Sanskrit classics, Freedom struggle memoirs, and contemporary Booker and Sahitya Akademi prize-winners.
concept: Frequently asked category covering classical works (Arthashastra by Chanakya, Shakuntala by Kalidasa, Rajatarangini by Kalhana), independence-era literature (Discovery of India by Nehru, Hind Swaraj by Gandhi, Anandamath by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay), and modern Booker winners (Arundhati Roy, Aravind Adiga, Salman Rushdie, Geetanjali Shree).

facts.title: Rajatarangini: History of Kashmir
facts.content: Written in Sanskrit verse by Kalhana in 1148-1150 CE, considered India's first systematic historical chronicle.

facts.title: Ashtadhyayi: Foundation of Sanskrit Grammar
facts.content: Composed by ancient grammarian Panini around the 5th-6th century BCE, defining 3,959 sutras on phonology and morphology.

mcqs.q: Who authored the famous novel 'Anandamath', which contains India's national song 'Vande Mataram'?
mcqs.exp: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay published Anandamath in 1882 based on the Sannyasi Rebellion.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'The Discovery of India' while imprisoned by the British at Ahmednagar Fort between 1942 and 1946?
mcqs.exp: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote the classic text surveying Indian culture, philosophy, and history during his detention.
